newsitem.title: KENYA: Somali faction leaders agree to end fighting.
newsitem.headline: Somali faction leaders agree to end fighting.

text.p: Main Somali faction leaders on Tuesday declared an end to hostilities in their country at the end of one week of talks at the invitation of Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi, the Kenyan government said.

The leaders included Hussein Aideed and Ali Mahdi Mohamed and agreed to allow free movement of people in Mogadishu and to remove all roadblocks leading from one region to another in the divided Somali capital, the government said in a statement.

It was not immediately known whether Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine who took over from his father Mohamed Farah Aideed following his death in Mogadishu on August 1, and Ali Mahdi held a face-to-face meeting.
Aideed, like his father, was elected president of Somalia by supporters and heads a government. But it has not received international recognition and is rejected by Ali Mahdi and other warlords.

The government statement said the Somali leaders came to the following understanding: - Declared cessation of hostilities, including media propaganda with immediate effect. - Allow free movement of people in the capital Mogadishu and remove all roadblocks leading from one region to another.

- Facilitate humanitarian delivery of aid to the people of Somalia. - Pledged continued dialogue in Somalia for a peace process and preserve the unity, sovereignity and the terrotorial integrity of Somalia.
